309-rhymes-of-a-rolling-stone.title: Rhymes Of A Rolling Stone
309-rhymes-of-a-rolling-stone.creator: Robert W. Service
309-rhymes-of-a-rolling-stone.description: A book by Robert W. Service. Still in me leaps the wonder of the boy,  A pride in man, a deathless faith in woman. Still red blood calls, still rings the valiant fray;  Adventure beacons through the summer gloaming:  Oh long and long and long will be the day  Ere I come homing!_

51599-what-we-saw-at-madame-world-s-fair.title: At Home
51599-what-we-saw-at-madame-world-s-fair.creator: Unknown
51599-what-we-saw-at-madame-world-s-fair.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. _Madame World said so much about it, that one of her older daughters tried to get the work done, without success, and, finally, Uncle Sam said, “Very well, Mother, I believe you are right about this; and though I am your very youngest son, if you will let me try, I promise you that I will cut a canal through that swampy back yard of yours, and that your biggest ships shall float safely through.”_

arxiv-1605-06319.title: As Cool as a Cucumber: Towards a Corpus of Contemporary Similes in Serbian
arxiv-1605-06319.description: Abstract Similes are natural language expressions used to compare unlikely things, where the comparison is not taken literally. They are often used in everyday communication and are an important part of cultural heritage. Having an up-to-date corpus of similes is challenging, as they are constantly coined and/or adapted to the contemporary times.

arxiv-2206-07329.title: Application-Oriented Selection of Privacy Enhancing Technologies Thanks: The final publication is available at link.springer.com ( https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-07315-1_5 ) Affiliation: Fraunhofer AISEC
arxiv-2206-07329.creator: Immanuel Kunz, Andreas Binder
arxiv-2206-07329.description: Abstract To create privacy-friendly software designs, architects need comprehensive knowledge of existing privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) and their properties. Existing works that systemize PETs, however, are outdated or focus on comparison criteria rather than providing guidance for their practical selection. In this short paper we present an enhanced classification of PETs that is more application-oriented than previous proposals.

arxiv-2209-05283.title: A UV census of the environments of stripped-envelope supernovae 2022 A UV census of the environments of stripped-envelope supernovae – References
arxiv-2209-05283.creator: Ning-Chen Sun, Justyn R. Maund, Paul A. Crowther1 School of Astronomy and Space Science, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, 19A Yuquan Road, Shijingshan District, Beijing 100049, China2 National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences, 20A Datun Road, Chaoyang District, Beiji
arxiv-2209-05283.description: Abstract This paper reports an environmental analysis of 41 uniformly-selected stripped-envelope supernovae (SESNe) based on deep ultraviolet-optical images acquired by the Hubble Space Telescope. Young stellar populations are detected in most SN environments and their ages are derived with a hierarchical Bayesian approach.

arxiv-2211-07853.title: Topological Transitions with an Imaginary Aubry-André-Harper Potential
arxiv-2211-07853.creator: Bofeng Zhu, Li-Jun Lang, Qiang Wang, Qi Jie Wang, Y. D. Chong
arxiv-2211-07853.description: Abstract We study one-dimensional lattices with imaginary-valued Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) potentials. Such lattices can host edge states with purely imaginary eigenenergies, which differ from the edge states of the Hermitian AAH model and are stabilized by a non-Hermitian particle-hole symmetry. The edge states arise when the period of the imaginary potential is a multiple of four lattice constants.

arxiv-2212-05566.title: YoloCurvSeg: You Only Label One Noisy Skeleton for Vessel-style Curvilinear Structure Segmentation Journal: Medical Image Analysis
arxiv-2212-05566.creator: Li Lin, Linkai Peng, Huaqing He, Pujin Cheng, Jiewei Wu, Kenneth K. Y. Wong, Xiaoying Tang
arxiv-2212-05566.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Li Lin, Linkai Peng, Huaqing He, Pujin Cheng, Jiewei Wu, Kenneth K. Y. Wong, Xiaoying Tang. Weakly-supervised learning (WSL) has been proposed to alleviate the conflict between data annotation cost and model performance through employing sparsely-grained (i.e., point-, box-, scribble-wise) supervision and has shown promising performance, particularly in the image segmentation field. However, it is still a very challenging task due to the limited supervision, especially when only a small number of labeled samples are available.

arxiv-2306-11161.title: Neuro-Symbolic Bi-Directional Translation - Deep Learning Explainability for Climate Tipping Point Research
arxiv-2306-11161.creator: Chace Ashcraft, Jennifer Sleeman, Caroline Tang, Jay Brett, Anand Gnanadesikan
arxiv-2306-11161.description: Abstract In recent years, there has been an increase in using deep learning for climate and weather modeling. Though results have been impressive, explainability and interpretability of deep learning models are still a challenge. A third wave of Artificial Intelligence (AI), which includes logic and reasoning, has been described as a way to address these issues.

arxiv-2403-04095.title: Helmholtz preconditioning for the compressible Euler equations using mixed finite elements with Lorenz staggering
arxiv-2403-04095.creator: David Lee, Alberto F. Martín, Kieran Ricardo
arxiv-2403-04095.description: Abstract Implicit solvers for atmospheric models are often accelerated via the solution of a preconditioned system. For block preconditioners this typically involves the factorisation of the (approximate) Jacobian resulting from linearization of the coupled system into a Helmholtz equation for some function of the pressure.

arxiv-2407-20181.title: Blockchain for Large Language Model Security and Safety: A Holistic Survey
arxiv-2407-20181.creator: Caleb Geren Amanda Board ∗ Gaby G. Dagher, Tim Andersen, Jun Zhuang
arxiv-2407-20181.description: Abstract With the growing development and deployment of large language models (LLMs) in both industrial and academic fields, their security and safety concerns have become increasingly critical. However, recent studies indicate that LLMs face numerous vulnerabilities, including data poisoning, prompt injections, and unauthorized data exposure, which conventional methods have struggled to address fully.

arxiv-2410-00873.title: EvalAssist : Insights on Task-Specific Evaluations and AI-Assisted Judgment Strategy Preferences
arxiv-2410-00873.creator: Zahra Ashktorab, Michael Desmond, Qian Pan, James M. Johnson, Martin Santillan Cooper, Elizabeth M. Daly, Rahul Nair, Tejaswini Pedapati, Hyo Jin Do, Werner Geyer
arxiv-2410-00873.description: Abstract . With the broad availability of large language models and their ability to generate vast outputs using varied prompts and configurations, determining the best output for a given task requires an intensive evaluation process, one where machine learning practitioners must decide how to assess the outputs and then carefully carry out the evaluation.

arxiv-2504-08071.title: Photon Excess from Dark Matter and Neutrino Scattering at MiniBooNE and MicroBooNE
arxiv-2504-08071.creator: Bhaskar Dutta, Aparajitha Karthikeyan, Doojin Kim, Adrian Thompson, Richard G. Van de Water
arxiv-2504-08071.description: Abstract We propose new solutions to accommodate both the MiniBooNE electron-like and MicroBooNE photon low-energy excesses, based on interactions involving light dark matter and/or neutrinos. The novelty of our proposal lies in the utilization of a photon arising from 2-to-3 scattering processes between a nucleus/nucleon and a neutrino and/or dark matter via exchanges of light mediators.

arxiv-2504-17578.title: Advancing CMA-ES with Learning-Based Cooperative Coevolution for Scalable Optimization
arxiv-2504-17578.creator: Hongshu Guo, Wenjie Qiu, Zeyuan Ma, Xinglin Zhang, Jun Zhang, Yue-Jiao Gong*
arxiv-2504-17578.description: Abstract . Recent research in Cooperative Coevolution (CC) have achieved promising progress in solving large-scale global optimization problems. However, existing CC paradigms have a primary limitation in that they require deep expertise for selecting or designing effective variable decomposition strategies.

arxiv-2507-00689.title: Polyakov loop model with exact static quark determinant in the ’t Hooft-Veneziano limit: U(N) case
arxiv-2507-00689.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . I investigate a three-dimensional U ⁡ ( N ) U(N) Polyakov loop model derived that includes the exact static determinant with N f N_{f} degenerate quark flavor and depends explicitly on the quark mass and chemical potential. In the large N , N f N,N_{f} limit mean field gives the exact solution, and the core of the Polyakov loop model is reduced to a deformed unitary matrix model, which I solve exactly.

arxiv-2510-10352.title: Osmotic forces modify lipid membrane fluctuations
arxiv-2510-10352.creator: Amaresh Sahu ‡
arxiv-2510-10352.description: Abstract . In hydrodynamic descriptions of lipid bilayers, the membrane is often approximated as being impermeable to the surrounding, solute-containing fluid. However, biological and in vitro lipid membranes are influenced by their permeability and the resultant osmotic forces—whose effects remain poorly understood.

arxiv-2604-26018.title: QERNEL: a Scalable Large Electron Model
arxiv-2604-26018.creator: Khachatur Nazaryan, Liang Fu

pmc-10541416.title: Cerebral endothelial cell-derived extracellular vesicles regulate microglial polarization and promote autophagy via delivery of miR-672-5p
pmc-10541416.creator: Changshui Wang, Lei Feng, Li Zhu, Linlin Wu, Beibei Chen, Changmeng Cui, Mengqi Yang, Yahao Gao, Pei Jiang
pmc-10541416.description: The interaction between cerebral endothelial cells (CEC) and brain parenchymal cells is critical to maintain neurovascular homeostasis, whereas extracellular vesicles (EVs) are essential to mediate the cell–cell communication. Previous researches demonstrated that CEC-derived EVs (CEC-EVs) confer neuroprotective actions. However, the molecular mechanisms remain unknown.

pmc-10697883.title: Understanding the diagnosis of superior mesenteric artery syndrome: analysis of the location of duodenal impression on upper gastrointestinal studies
pmc-10697883.creator: Scott Caterine, Nikhil S. Patil, Heba Takrouri, Robert M. Issenman, Nina R. Stein, John Donnellan, Ali Yikilmaz
pmc-10697883.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundUpper gastrointestinal (GI) contrast studies are frequently requested to aid superior mesenteric artery syndrome diagnosis, a rare entity. Compression of the third duodenal part is expected to be mid-to-left of the midline where the superior mesenteric artery arises from the aorta; however, a duodenal impression to the right of the midline due to normal anatomic impression by the inferior vena cava (IVC) is often encountered and frequently misdiagnosed.ObjectiveThe purpose of this study was to determine the frequencies of (1) normal right-of-midline duodenal

pmc-11547006.title: Wound Healing, Anti-Inflammatory and Anti-Oxidant Activities, and Chemical Composition of Korean Propolis from Different Sources
pmc-11547006.creator: Aman Dekebo, Chalshisa Geba, Daniel Bisrat, Jin Boo Jeong, Chuleui Jung, Maria da Graça Costa G Miguel, Ofélia Anjos
pmc-11547006.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Propolis, such as is used as bio-cosmetics and in functional materials, is increasing because of its antioxidant medicinal benefits. However, its pharmacological and chemical composition is highly variable, relative to its geography and botanical origins. Comparative studies on three propolis samples collected from different regions in Korea have been essential for linking its provenance, chemical composition, and biological activity, thereby ensuring the efficient utilization of its beneficial properties.

pmc-11603829.title: Using normalisation process theory to evaluate the implementation of a digital health intervention in community and secondary care long COVID clinics
pmc-11603829.creator: Fiona A Stevenson, Paul Pfeffer, Sarah Walker, Hadiza Ismaila, Vinosh Jegatheesan, Ibrahim Mohammad, Ann Blandford, Stuart Linke, John R Hurst, William Ricketts, Fiona L Hamilton, David Sunkersing, Katherine Bradbury, Henry Goodfellow
pmc-11603829.description: ObjectivesThe potential and expected benefits of digital health interventions (DHI) have long been discussed, yet substantial challenges are associated with deploying DHI at scale. Insights are presented concerning the implementation of a DHI consisting of a patient-facing app and a digital dashboard for clinicians providing supported self-management for long COVID to support both clinicians and patients.

pmc-12648870.title: SMARCB1 (INI-1) deficient vulvar neoplasms: report of 4 cases with review of literature
pmc-12648870.creator: Meenakshi Kamboj, Prerna Chadha, Anila Sharma, Sarika Gupta, Vandana Jain, Divya Bansal, Sunil Pasricha, Gurudutt Gupta, Garima Durga, Anurag Mehta
pmc-12648870.description: SMARCB1 (INI-1) deficient vulvar neoplasms are rare tumors with scarce available literature. These tumors can be comprised of proximal type epithelioid sarcoma (ES), myoepithelial carcinoma (MEC), myoepithelioma-like tumor of the vulvar region (MELTVR), and myxoepithelioid tumor with chordoid features (METC). A subset of vulvar yolk sac tumors (VYSTs) also exhibit INI-1 deficiency.

pmc-12709131.title: Comparison of multispectral singlet oxygen luminescence dosimetry and singlet oxygen explicit dosimetry in artificial phantom
pmc-12709131.creator: Weibing Yang, Baozhu Lu, Madelyn Johnson, Dennis Sourvanos, Hongjing Sun, Andreea Dimofte, Vikas Vikas, Robert H. Hadfield, Brian C. Wilson, Timothy C. Zhu
pmc-12709131.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). .SignificanceDirect detection of singlet-state oxygen (O12) is a critical objective in Type II photodynamic therapy (PDT) due to its pivotal role in mediating therapeutic effects. Although multispectral singlet oxygen dosimetry (MSOLD) has demonstrated the capability to detect O12 luminescence both in vitro and in vivo, there remains no standardized method for accurately quantifying reactive singlet oxygen, [O2]rx1, based on these measured signals. By contrast, the singlet oxygen explicit dosimetry (SOED) model offers a robust framework for calculating [O2]rx1.

pmc-12968316.title: Reliability and Construct Validity of the Physician's Global Assessment of Lung Disease in Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis–Associated Lung Disease
pmc-12968316.creator: Eileen Rife, Guihua Zhai, Mekibib Altaye, Jennifer Andringa, Hermine I. Brunner, Scott Canna, Lauren A. Henderson, Yukiko Kimura, Scott M. Lieberman, Mona Riskalla, Christopher Towe, Tiphanie Vogel, Holly Wobma, Grant Schulert, Rabheh Abdul Aziz, Rabheh Abdul Aziz, Sheila Angeles‐Han, Kevin Baszis,
pmc-12968316.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThe physician global assessment of lung disease (PGALD) is a recently proposed disease activity measure for patients with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis–associated lung disease (SJIA‐LD). This study evaluates the reliability and construct validity of the PGALD.MethodsFifty‐seven pediatric rheumatologists and pulmonologists with experience caring for children with SJIA‐LD were invited to rate 20 clinical vignettes using the PGALD, a 10‐point Likert scale (0 = inactive SJIA‐LD; 10 = highly active SJIA‐LD). Raters were also asked to rate a subset of eight repeat vignettes.

pmc-13206428.title: Genome‐Wide Assessment Reveals Ancestral Differences in Homozygosity Patterns Potentially Linked to Parkinson's Disease Etiology
pmc-13206428.creator: Kathryn Step, Carlos F Hernández, Marzieh Khani, Esraa Eltaraifee, Ana Jimena Hernández‐Medrano, Pin‐Jui Kung, Miriam Ostrožovičová, Alexandra Zirra, Eduardo Pérez‐Palma, Niccolò E Mencacci, Ignacio J Keller Sarmiento, Huw R Morris, Ignacio F Mata, Juliana Acosta‐Uribe, Zih‐Hua Fang, Sara Bandres‐Ci
pmc-13206428.description: BackgroundRecessive genetic variation and extended runs of homozygosity (ROHs) may contribute to the unexplained heritability of Parkinson's disease (PD), particularly in diverse and understudied populations.ObjectiveWe conducted the first large‐scale, multi‐ancestral investigation of PD to examine the impact of genome‐wide homozygosity on disease risk and age at onset (AAO).

pmc-13415589.title: Hierarchical vision mamba U-net for farmland semantic segmentation from remote sensing imagery
pmc-13415589.creator: Jing Zhang, Ting Zhang, Guohong Qi
pmc-13415589.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Farmland semantic segmentation (FSS) from remote sensing imagery (RSIs) is a critical yet challenging task in precision agriculture. CNN-based methods suffer from limited receptive fields and poor long-range dependency modeling, while Transformers are limited by quadratic computational complexity.

pmc-13518970.title: Graphite lubricates Mercury’s global contraction
pmc-13518970.creator: Natalia A VERGARA SASSARINI, Matteo MASSIRONI, Telemaco TESEI, Andrea BISTACCHI
pmc-13518970.description: Secular cooling of Mercury’s interior drove planetary contraction, forming widespread lobate scarps that are the surface expressions of thrust faults and fold-and-thrust belts. Despite their importance to Mercury’s global tectonics, the mechanics and rheology of these features remain poorly understood.

uslaw-usc-t10-s9622.title: 10 U.S.C. § 9622 — Rations: commissioned officers in field
uslaw-usc-t10-s9622.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s9622.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part IV (Service, Supply, And Procurement); Chapter 969 (Sale Of Serviceable Material). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Commissioned officers of the Air Force and commissioned officers of the Space Force serving in the field may buy rations for their own use, on credit. Amounts due for these purchases shall be reported monthly to the Secretary.
